independent_review.text:
# Independent review: radio nullable ARIA eba6

The bounded three-input type widening is supported, subject to a current-tree comparison and separate radio authored-use source-epoch requalification. Candidate `e06654e2f088c21d25a209f1f48c1cc725f295fe`, base `0d7ca9de354a974520a7ecc76607a2827befa57d`, patch SHA256 `ec6e838c8083b6086c2b9e889073e35c8fec25d97a70b7adde0707988353030d`. The complete upstream `eba6ee844b8e8e6044e1675b5e41ff13224ead75` widens the same three radio ARIA input types to nullable and adds null-reset tests. Material 16 declared strings; this candidate is an explicit conservative TypeScript compatibility widening, not historical declaration identity.

I independently ran the strict Angular AOT fixture against the retained extracted baseline and candidate packages: baseline fails with exactly three `TS2322` nullable binding errors, candidate succeeds, and a candidate control with numeric aria-label fails with one `TS2322`. The fixture binds all three values through a public radio template, with strict templates and strict null checks. Logs in this directory: old SHA256 `5697c4489b762caedc79e96b299b9366eef0410eb0b4152bb3a63d009ed4c281`, new `e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855`, number control `7027db226baf0dec6b9b4b278f8caf71f83070f956efbf21bc5b8656031be867`. The control exercises a number on aria-label, not each separate input.

Independently compared every regular member of both tarballs against the extracted test packages: 512/512 match for each. Baseline tar SHA256 `2cf96975b6f6adaa83a8bf42f99a756f34bbdd7166ea899120f5605c66f8bffb`, candidate `b42bd87238076488f0fd7bf5ff7b7e61d4a781c8988e02647e0bdd9109e7806c`. Between archives the radio runtime FESM is byte-identical; only its FESM map, declaration and declaration map differ, and the complete declaration diff consists of the three `string | null` widenings. No template, CSS or Sass changed.

The retained packed candidate TestBed report SHA256 `05685b9d0ff1a14c74b088f9a8bdcee86bcf500906909f481fcbfcb28266d66e` passed 100/100; the same candidate tests against the extracted baseline, report SHA256 `542c318ed445fcef5fd685bebb15ef7fbb794ba4ea7efd476c502fd0de9f38a8`, also passed 100/100. They verify all three native attributes through value→null→value→undefined. Thus the runtime removal was already present; the demonstrated fix is strict template typing. The baseline report has null artifact SHA but the independent complete extraction comparison connects it to the old tar. Candidate records source unchanged and the run's artifact SHA matches its tar.

No independent browser replay was performed. The isolated worktree links the canonical pinned installation instead of a fresh install; previous bootstrap probes were inconclusive and are not counted. No strict no-Zone, x64, 21.x, full suite, security or release qualification follows. Preserve old reports and do not treat this type-only patch as an automatic 28-row source-epoch update.
